findings.title: enableSqlExpressions evaluates an inverted feature flag and then ignores it
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` on both branches. Two problems: (1) the variable named `enabled` is actually true when the flag is *disabled*, so if anyone later re-enables the feature by changing the final `return false` to `return enabled`, SQL expressions would be enabled exactly when the flag is off; (2) the flag lookup is dead code that misleads readers into thinking the flag still controls the behaviour. If the intent is a hard kill-switch, the function should simply return false with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264; if the intent is to keep the flag, the negation must be removed.

findings.title: Users of the legacy SQL node path get a misleading 'invalid sql query' error instead of 'not implemented'
findings.body: `NewSQLCommand` is still reachable through `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (the `rawNode` / classic graph path), which is not gated by the new `enableSqlExpressions` check in reader.go. On that path the stubbed `sql.TablesList` now always fails with `not implemented`, but the code wraps it as `logger.Warn("invalid sql query", ...)` and returns a BadRequest with public message `error reading SQL command`. Users who had SQL expressions in dashboards/alert rules will be told their SQL is invalid rather than that the feature has been disabled, which will generate confusing support reports. The stub error should be detected and surfaced as a clear 'SQL expressions are disabled' message.

findings.title: No tests cover the new 'SQL expressions always rejected' behaviour
findings.body: This PR changes `pkg/expr/sql` so that `TablesList`, `RunCommands` and `QueryFramesInto` always return errors, and adds a gate in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` that rejects `QueryTypeSQL`. No test is added or updated to assert that a SQL expression query is rejected via either entry point (`ReadQuery` or `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand`), nor that it stays rejected when `FlagSqlExpressions` is enabled. Given this is the in-repo landing of a critical CVE fix, a regression test is needed so a future refactor (e.g. 'fixing' the dead-code in `enableSqlExpressions`) cannot silently re-expose the feature. Any pre-existing tests in `pkg/expr/sql` that exercised `TablesList` against a working engine would also now fail and should be updated or removed in this PR.
